title: Canary simulation retro & operational planning notes
body:
Overview:
This document captures facilitator notes, post-lab retro observations, and an operationalization plan from a customer-facing canary simulation lab. It is intended to be a lightweight working artifact that the SE team and the customer SRE can iterate on after the workshop.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
We ran a two-hour lab with the customer to compare three routing approaches: (1) region-preferring full-precision models, (2) weight-based mix with quantized fallbacks, and (3) remote-hosted overflow. The simulation showed that a conservative canary (5%-25% over 3 phases) with an explicit KV cache warm-up reduced p95 spikes and kept p99 under the SLA while delivering a ~18% cost reduction versus the full fp16 baseline. Key unresolved items: human quality checks for edge cases, egress cost guardrails for cross-region overflow, and a tailored alerting threshold for cache miss storms.

Facilitator notes (what worked):
- Short primer slides with visuals helped align stakeholders quickly. Keep these under 6 slides.
- Real-time metric capture (shared sheet) enabled faster synthesis than switching between dashboards.
- Two breakout prompts (latency-first and cost-first) produced complementary policy candidates.

Facilitator notes (what to improve next run):
- Provide a pre-seeded human-eval sample set for quality checks to avoid ad-hoc sampling.
- Include an example of a bad canary run (intentional failure) so teams practice rollback.
- Bring a lightweight cost calc sheet prefilled with model $/1M token rows.

Recommended artifacts to deliver after the workshop (priority order):
1) Canonical policy YAMLs (control, latency-first, cost-first) with comments and owner fields.
2) Canary runbook: phases, monitoring queries, and explicit rollback commands.
3) Dashboard exports: route-level latency histograms, token cost time-series, cache-hit rate.
4) Small human-eval checklist and a sample rubric for assessing quality regressions.
5) Tickets for infra to provision the canary pool and for security to review network egress.

Operational plan (steps, owners, and dates):
- Day 0 (staging prep) owner: infra-team: provision 3-node canary pool, enable metrics collection (deadline: +3 business days)
- Day 1 (smoke) owner: SE + customer SRE: run baseline generator for 1 hour, verify dashboards (+1 day after prep)
- Day 2-4 (phase 1) owner: customer SRE: ramp to 5% traffic to canary; monitor p95/p99, cache-hit; daily check-ins
- Day 5-12 (phase 2) owner: product + SE: expand to 25% if no regressions; collect human eval samples
- Day 13-30 (phase 3) owner: infra + eng: expand to 50% and confirm cost targets; run retrospective at day 30

Monitoring & alerting recommendations (examples):
- Alert A: route_p99_latency > SLA * 1.25 for 5m -> page on-call, trigger immediate 50% rollback to control route
- Alert B: cache_hit_rate drops > 15% vs baseline for 10m -> send notification, run quick KV warm-up script
- Alert C: cross_region_egress_cost > monthly_budget_rate * 1.2 -> pause remote overflow routing and notify billing owner

Decision matrix template (to be filled by customer during handoff):
- Metric (p95/p99/cost/quality) | Acceptable delta | Action if breached | Owner | Escalation path
- Example row: p99 | +20ms | rollback to previous weight distribution | customer SRE | SE oncall

Quality evaluation plan:
- Synthetic checks: automated diff on outputs for a holdout test set (weighted by business-critical intents).
- Human checks: 50 sampled responses per phase with rubric: correctness, hallucination risk, terse vs verbose behavior.
- Trigger thresholds: if human score delta > 4 points (out of 100) -> immediate rollback and investigate.

Cost considerations noted during lab:
- Quantized models show lower token-cost but occasionally increase token consumption due to longer outputs; measure cost per useful-answer not just per token.
- Remote overflow can incur unpredictable egress fees; set absolute max % of traffic routed remotely as a policy field.

Post-workshop retro action items (team assignments):
- SE: commit policy YAMLs to shared repo and add comments (owner: Sofia Patel, due +3 days)
- Infra: provision canary pool and export dashboard templates (owner: Diego Alvarez, due +5 days)
- Customer SRE: schedule first smoke run and invite SE to daily standups for first 72 hrs (owner: Hannah Brooks, due +7 days)
- Product: define quality acceptance criteria and sign-off process for canary (owner: product lead, due +10 days)

Appendix: useful commands and snippets (text):
- Warm-up KV cache: python tools/warm_kv.py --model model-A --duration 300
- Run traffic profile: python tools/traffic_gen.py --profile steady --qps 80 --duration 3600 --seed 123
- Export dashboard: redwoodctl export-dashboard --name "canary-route" --out canary-dashboard.json
- Example small policy YAML header (to be expanded in repo):
  name: "customer-canary-1"
  owner: "customer-sre@acme.com"
  routes: [control, canary]

Notes for the SE facilitator when wrapping up:
- Confirm owners and dates in calendar invites before the final 10 minutes of the session.
- Ask the customer to identify a single decision-maker for post-canary go/no-go.
- Leave a simple 2-question survey for attendees (did this change your confidence to proceed? what concerns remain?).

End of notes.
